coverage_gaps: The visible Layer 1B candidate data is concentrated in transmission hardware, utility structures, transformer/power-quality equipment, HVDC/reactive-power equipment, and nuclear fuel-cycle nodes; oil and gas remains under-decomposed.

A separate oil and gas branch should map LNG power demand, gas turbines, compression, backup generation, pipeline constraints, produced-water/power-electrification suppliers, and distributed generation for data-center reliability.

Renewables-specific nodes remain incomplete: inverters, grid-forming controls, substation automation, switchgear, protection relays, cable accessories, medium-voltage equipment, and interconnection queue bottlenecks need additional candidate expansion.

Live market caps, liquidity, analyst coverage, valuation, short interest, and ownership concentration were not fully verified for every candidate in this merge; market-cap buckets are inherited from supplied context where available and otherwise marked unknown.

International candidates such as Quality Power Electrical Equipments require exchange-ticker verification, local filings, liquidity checks, governance review, and currency/listing-risk assessment before promotion.
Nuclear conversion appears to be a real bottleneck but lacks clean pure-play public exposure; Honeywell is included only as a reference because the relevant asset is likely too diluted.

Private or embedded competitors remain important for later falsification: MacLean Power Systems in transmission hardware, X-energy in TRISO fuel fabrication, private transformer/switchgear suppliers, and grid OEM subcomponents inside mega-cap divisions.
No current filing-level validation has yet been completed for backlog, customer concentration, margin quality, capacity additions, certification status, or lead-time claims.

Utility regulatory evidence is still needed: FERC transmission rules, DOE grid programs, NRC licensing, utility IRPs, PJM/capacity-market developments, interconnection queues, and procurement filings.

The current universe may still underrepresent software/data/certification bottlenecks, testing and inspection vendors, distributors, and specialty component suppliers one or two steps away from obvious power demand.

memory_update.text: Energy Layer 1 universe should prioritize infrastructure chokepoints rather than treating the theme only as commodity exposure, utilities, or mega-cap power headlines.

Transmission-line hardware remains one of the strongest underfollowed Energy nodes because it is procured before construction completion and has narrow public exposure through PLPC with Hubbell as a diversified comp.

Dry-type transformers, power-quality products, and magnetics are high-priority nodes because AI data centers, industrial electrification, renewables, microgrids, and aging grid infrastructure all require reliable power distribution and conditioning.
Utility structures and second-order processing nodes such as galvanizing may offer underfollowed exposure to transmission buildout when direct electrical-equipment names are already well covered.

HVDC/reactive-power equipment and high-voltage power-quality systems should remain in the Energy funnel, especially for renewable integration and long-distance bulk power transfer, but international candidates require local filing and liquidity verification.

Nuclear fuel-cycle research must keep uranium mining separate from conversion, enrichment, HALEU, and advanced fuel fabrication; several of the tightest bottlenecks are private or embedded inside diversified mega-caps.
Oil and gas requires a separate Layer 1B expansion covering LNG, gas turbines, compression, backup generation, pipeline constraints, and data-center reliability demand.

Later layers must verify market cap, liquidity, analyst coverage, backlog, customer concentration, capacity expansion, margin quality, certification status, and current valuation before promoting any candidate from Layer 1 universe to ranked thesis.

summary: Layer 1C merged the available Energy Layer 1A theme map and visible Layer 1B node-level candidates into a deduplicated Serenity universe. The strongest current universe is biased toward grid equipment, transmission hardware, transformer/power-quality equipment, HVDC/reactive-power systems, and nuclear fuel-cycle/component bottlenecks. The highest-priority underfollowed names are narrow suppliers or second-order chokepoints whose products are schedule-critical but less visible than utilities, hyperscalers, mega-cap OEMs, or EPC contractors. This is a research universe only, not a buy/sell recommendation.
